courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will become familiar with all aspects of safety that must be complied with when working in a Machine Shop environment. The course will focus on safe work practices, hazardous materials and WHMIS regulations, WorkSafeBC requirements, fire safety, as well as the proper methods of lifting and moving objects. Students must complete this course before participating in any shop floor activities. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course students will learn the necessary mathematic skills they need to support machining operations. The mathematical knowledge students will acquire during this course will support all subjects covered in the machinist trades training programs. As they work through the course, students will develop research skills and access reference literature found in the Machinery’s Handbook. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course guides students through the process of reading and interpreting basic engineering drawings. Students will learn to effectively communicate by reading and creating sketches of an object in several views. Also the students will be able to describe fits and tolerances. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course students will learn to use and maintain basic hand tools according to safety requirements. Students will select, use and properly maintain layout and measuring tools and gauges. Students will learn to identify fasteners and their application. Both metric and imperial measurement systems will be used. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will learn how to safely use a drill press, power saw, grinding machine and hydraulic press to perform machining operations to drawing specifications. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will learn engine lathes and basic lathe operations. The focus of the course will be on providing students with hands on experience and basic expertise in various lathe operations. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students learn the basic skills needed to operate vertical and horizontal milling machines including tooling, appropriate cutting speeds, feed, depth of cut, accessories and holding devices. The course also will cover the set-up procedure for general machine operation, and explore the causes of cutter failure. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students learn how to cut internal and external threads using an engine lathe. They will work with multiple types of thread forms to achieve different thread designations. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will learn to use rotary tables and indexing devices to perform milling machine operations. They will learn to set up accessories for the milling machine to cut radii, hexagonal and pentagonal shapes according to specifications. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will learn about different types of metals and their chemical, mechanical and physical properties. Students will learn to identify steel and common metals, and modify steel properties through various heat treating processes. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will learn how to select the correct lubricants and hydraulic fluids for various types of equipment. Students will be introduced to the different types of bearings, seals and gaskets found in machines. The course covers lubrication requirements of varying types of bearings. Students will also select cutting fluids for specific machining applications. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students learn the basics about precision surface grinding. Students will select the correct grinding wheels for specific applications, identify methods of surface grinding and articulate the advantages of each method. Students will also learn to safely operate and maintain surface grinders. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course prepares students to find employment in the machinist trade. Students will learn how to write a cover letter and resume to detail their experience and learning accomplishments. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will learn basic skills in oxyacetylene cutting and welding. Students will work in a welding shop environment to learn the basics about equipment components and their safe handling. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course students are introduced to computer numerical control (CNC) machines and the theory behind their operation. Topics covered include: types of machines, their operation, as well as machine components and tooling. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will plan machining procedures to complete an assembly project. Students will comply with safety practices on all machinery in the machine shop and build project components using the skills they have learned in previous courses. The students will machine the components according to the engineering drawings’ specifications and assemble them to complete the project. The assembly project will include threaded components and surface finish requirements. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: Successful complete of all Level 1 courses.
courses.course_overview_raw: Prerequisite(s): Successful complete of all Level 1 courses.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Deals with key concepts such as machine construction, NC v. CNC, coordinate systems and reference points. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: A general overview of manual part programming is covered including functions such as data input, coordinate system presets and tool offsets. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: A more detailed application of lathe programming principals and includes concepts such as canned and multiple repetitive cycles. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: A more detailed application of machine centre programming principles and includes concepts such as drilling, tapping and boring cycles. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course is a practical application of turning centre setup and operation. Home position, work coordinates, tool offsets, screen reading, tool setup and job holding are covered. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course is a practical application of machine centre setup and operation. Home position, work coordinates, tool offsets, screen reading, tool setup and job holding are covered. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course covers basic concepts of 2-D and 3-D geometry creation and editing in Mastercam. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Basic 2-D and 3-D tool path creation, tool path editing, post processing, job setup and part machining are covered. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course covers the basic functions of the coordinate measuring machine and will allow the student to accurately measure and record finished parts. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

admission.raw: Find out more about getting started in the program! If the CNC Machinist program interests you, review the entrance requirements. If you qualify, you may want to attend an information session or become a student for a day. Spend-A-Day with us Want to learn more about our program before you apply? Come Spend-A-Day with us. You’ll meet students and instructors, and get a hands-on feel for what the program is about. If you have questions regarding the entrance requirements or the application process, visit Admission & Registration or if you want to discuss the program in more detail, contact the Department Head, Stefano Pettenon , or call 604-432-8214. Scheduled intakes January and September *Scheduled intakes are subject to change Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of the following: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Pre-Calculus 11 (50%) or Foundations of Math 11 (60%) or Workplace Math 11 (67%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success Applicants should have: Good command of oral and written English Sufficient physical strength and stamina to meet the demands of the work, good hearing, good eyesight, normal colour vision, manual dexterity and hand/eye coordination Good theoretical and practical mathematical skills and mechanical aptitude Potential students with medical or physical difficulties should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview (telephone interview if out of town) with the institute's rehabilitation specialist at 604-451-6963. Trades Discovery The Trades Discovery General and Trades Discovery for Women are full-time programs designed to prepare participants to successfully enter and complete a Trades Training program. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
